items.text: Swarm-manager's GCT integration is a clean async pattern: trigger POST /api/v1/review/run → poll GET /review/run/{jobID} every 5s (10min timeout) → ReviewResult with classification (ready/ready_with_notes/needs_work/not_assessable) and 5 dimensions (codeQuality, tests, standards, visual, provenance), each scored green/yellow/red/skipped.

Ecosystem-manager currently has NO GCT integration. It tracks execution metadata (duration, prompt size, exit reason) and Auto Steer state (phase/iteration/steering source) via file-based JSON + PostgreSQL, but quality gates only use MetricsSnapshot (build status, operational targets) — not GCT review dimensions.

The natural integration point is IterationEvaluator.Evaluate() in autosteer/, which already runs after each iteration, increments counters, collects MetricsSnapshot, and evaluates phase stop conditions. A GCT review trigger could be inserted here.

GCT enforces a single-active-review-per-scenario constraint (409 Conflict). Reviews can take up to 5 minutes with all 3 checks (tidiness, tests, rules) running in parallel. The API supports selective checks and a 'details' parameter for lightweight requests.

items.context: Full GCT reviews take up to 5 minutes. Auto Steer iterations can be as short as a few minutes. Triggering a full review after every iteration could double cycle time. We need to decide how often to trigger reviews.

options.label: Review after every iteration
options.rationale: Maximum visibility into health trends, but doubles iteration time and may bottleneck on one-review-at-a-time constraint

options.label: Review only at phase boundaries
options.rationale: Minimal overhead — only runs when Auto Steer transitions phases. Misses intra-phase regressions but keeps iteration speed high

options.label: Lightweight per-iteration + full at phase boundaries
options.rationale: Run a fast subset (e.g., tidiness only) per iteration for trend data, and a full 5-dimension review at phase boundaries. Balances visibility with speed

options.label: Configurable frequency (every N iterations)
options.rationale: Let the Auto Steer profile specify review frequency. Most flexible but adds configuration complexity

items.context: Ecosystem-manager uses dual storage: file-based JSON (metadata.json per execution) and PostgreSQL (profile_execution_state, profile_executions). We need to decide where per-loop health snapshots live.

options.label: Enrich existing ExecutionHistory with review fields
options.rationale: Adds ReviewResult fields to the existing metadata.json and profile_executions tables. Simple, co-located with other execution data. Downside: bloats existing records, harder to query trends independently

options.label: New dedicated snapshot table + JSON files
options.rationale: A separate 'loop_health_snapshots' table with foreign key to task/execution. Clean separation, easy trend queries, supports standalone regression detection. Slightly more schema to maintain

options.label: Extend MetricsSnapshot with review dimensions
options.rationale: Add GCT dimensions to the existing MetricsSnapshot struct used by Auto Steer. Tight integration with phase stop conditions but couples review availability to metrics collection

items.context: Swarm-manager has a working HTTPReviewClient in its execution package. Ecosystem-manager needs similar functionality. Should it reuse the same code or have its own?

options.label: Copy and adapt swarm-manager's review_client.go
options.rationale: Fast to implement. Ecosystem-manager gets its own copy tailored to per-loop needs (e.g., different polling intervals, lightweight check support). Some code duplication

options.label: Extract shared review client to api-core library
options.rationale: Both swarm-manager and ecosystem-manager import from a shared library. DRY but adds cross-scenario dependency and coordination cost

options.label: Ecosystem-manager calls swarm-manager's review endpoint instead of GCT directly
options.rationale: Swarm-manager proxies the review. Avoids duplication but adds an intermediary hop and coupling between scenarios

plan_updates: Created initial conclusion scaffold with research question, methodology, and 5 findings covering the existing swarm-manager integration pattern, GCT API contract, ecosystem-manager's current state, natural integration points, and performance concerns.
